responses.response: Create the elements first. For the processing service, start with the create-element skill. For the production VM, start with the model-deployment-infrastructure skill. Once they exist, choose the description format by element type: for the service, use a prose description and add a metadata {} block only when you need queryable fields such as owner or regions; for the VM, use a Markdown table in the description for ops-readable specs, with optional metadata only if automation must query those values.

For ProdApiVm, use a single Markdown table in the description. Put network interfaces first, starting with eth0 and then eth1 if present, because operators need networking immediately. After that, list OS, then hardware such as CPU, RAM, GPU, and Disk, then service or runtime details such as container runtime or health check, then operational items such as RTO or backup notes if they matter. Do not duplicate the hostname because the VM title already gives it, do not put the normal gateway on the VM because that belongs to the zone, and do not repeat relationships such as firewall rules, monitoring links, or service endpoints that are already modeled elsewhere. Add a metadata block only if automation needs to query the same fields.

Keep ProdApiVm ops-useful by using one concise Markdown table and ordering it by actionability: eth0 first, then eth1 for monitoring, then OS, then hardware such as CPU, RAM, GPU, and Disk, then the small set of service or runtime details an operator truly needs, then key operational facts such as health check and RTO. Keep only information that helps someone run or recover the VM quickly. If details become too fine-grained, such as full package inventories, long tuning notes, driver matrices, or large runbooks, move those to separate operations documentation and leave only a short pointer from the model. Also avoid duplicating data that belongs elsewhere, such as gateway or VLAN details owned by the zone, or relationship-level information already shown in diagrams. Add metadata only when automation needs to query specific values.
